Maria: quick heads-up — ran a small preheat experiment during the last deploy window for redwood-2-14b. wanted to share numbers and get opinions on keying + autoscale interactions.
Maria: tl;dr: deploy-time ephemeral warmers (top-5 prefixes per region) bumped observed prefix hit-rate from ~11% -> ~42% for the warmed shards, but we saw p99 latency blips (~+18–25ms) coincident with autoscale events.
Sasha: can you paste the exact keying and how the warmers generate load?
Maria: keyed by (model, trunc_prefix_hash_v1, seq_len_bucket). used 64-bit farmhash and a simple rotation per shard to spread seeds. generator used parallel workers: ```./preheat --model redwood-2-14b --prefix-file top_prefixes.csv --parallel 8 --seq-buckets "8,32,128"```
Jake: noted. after the kernel-selector change last week we started using the tile-8 attention kernel by default for medium-length sequences — that reduced steady-state per-token time but introduced extra small memcpy ops when warming lots of short contexts. suspected cause for the tail blips.
Noah: i instrumented the harness — flame samples show: token_decode 42%, kv_copy 21%, scheduler_wait 10%. small buffer allocs spike during the initial burst and the python worker GC causes jitter.
Maria: right — we observed GC spikes. quick mitigation was switching the preheat harness to a long-lived worker pool with reuse of output buffers; that cut the jitter ~50% but didn't eliminate the p99 bump entirely.
Sasha: interesting. what's the cardinality of the prefix keyspace you seeded?
Maria: top_prefixes.csv was ~24k unique prefixes globally, but after hashing+shard rotation per-region we ended up doing ~6k distinct keys per shard.
Jake: that higher cardinality is part of it — more unique KV entries => more small allocations and more frequent KV page faults on the tile-8 path.
Sasha: proposals: 1) normalize keying to collapse equivalent prefixes (trim whitespace, lowercase, collapse repeated tokens) -> reduce cardinality. 2) move to fingerprint_v2 (64->48 bit) with deterministic bucketization to reduce per-shard uniqueness. 3) run preheat with a probabilistic top-K sampler (weight by recent traffic) instead of full enumerate.
Noah: +1 on probabilistic sampling. also: don't run full preheat at the same time as autoscale-up. if GPU util > 65% skip or backoff warmers. set a soft QS lock during scale events.
Maria: here's a short log snippet from the window (removed timestamps):
```
preheat: shard=3 seed_count=6123 issued=6123 pending=0 avg_rtt_ms=12.4 p50=9.1 p95=19.3 p99=46.2
kernel-selector: switched -> tile-8 for seq_len=64
workerpool: reused_buffers=4096 gc_pause_ms=32
autoscaler: scale_up start, new_nodes=2
preheat: observed p99 spike coincident with scale_up
```
Jake: actionable runway: add kernel-aware backoff in preheat: detect kernel-selector mode and avoid high-allocation paths (e.g., break synthetic requests into fewer, longer prefixes for tile-8); also add a bounded async allocator in the harness to avoid GC storms.
Sasha: and on keying: normalize on the client side before hashing. that should collapse about ~18% of the keys in top_prefixes.csv based on our quick dedupe run.
Maria: next steps (agreed):
- Maria: push keying normalization + fingerprint_v2 on the preheat generator (canary).
- Jake: implement kernel-aware backoff + bounded allocator in harness.
- Sasha: run 48h canary with rate limit 5rps per instance and probabilistic sampler; capture prefix hit-rate, p50/p95/p99, and GPU util.
- Noah: add autoscale-safe guard: if in scale-up window or GPU util > 65% then backoff preheat.
Noah: assigning tasks in GH: @Maria -> infra/preheat#412, @Jake -> runtime/warmers#88, @Sasha -> evals/prefill#59. check-in tomorrow 10:00am PT.
